followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the observed 23 March 2021 Busia freight protest, separate from the underlying maize commodity restriction. Traders and clearing agents obstructed trucks and customs documents in both directions. No universal passenger restriction is evidenced, and the movement obstruction is not represented as a state-ordered all-traffic closure. The Tuesday date supports 23 March onset and last confirmation. Several hours and later crisis meetings do not supply an observed reopening. Endpoint remains unknown; the zero-day lower bound is not a complete or exact operational duration. Trade and transport protest coding follows the participants’ complaints over maize restrictions, impounding and fines. The health reason for the underlying maize rule is not transferred to this protest as its rationale. The relevant Monitor paragraphs were freshly read before the registration wall. No inaccessible later content is recertified. The named reporter and the one source origin are retained; PIDA supplies geography only. PIDA E6 visually confirms 0.46555 / 34.09767 for the approved approximate Busia crossing marker. It is not the precise protest barricade or paperwork desk. Preserve freight-only interpretation and the last-confirmation display limit.

Keep all source-access, reporting-origin, geography, directional, policy/operational and uncertain-duration qualifications.
